body.statement: For \(\mathfrak G_4\) at \(r=2\), the exhibited rule \(Q_{49/25}\) is globally \(0.95\)-honest because \(2\Phi(-49/25)<0.049995791\), and \(\sup_{h\in H_2}E_h\ell\{Q_{49/25}(W)\}<3/4+\arctan(\sqrt{3/10})/(2\pi)-\{\Phi(1/25)-1/2\}<0.813799\). The exact atomic dual value \(L_4\) generated by \(\beta_4\) and \(\nu_4\) exceeds \(0.361100\); its whole-line scalar reduction charges less than \(3753/10^{15}\) for replacing the optimizing multiplier by \(\lambda_4\). At \(r=0\), common-contact coverage implies risk at least \(14/15\), and \(K_{\mathrm{ct}}\) attains \(14/15\).
body.justification: Every numerical bound now names the exact rule, atoms, weights, analytic reduction, and outward replacement charge needed for reproduction.
body.gap: No published paper studies this four-label fan, and the rigorous enclosure width remains \(0.452699\), far above the requested milliscale gap.
body.consumer: The explicit formulas are mandatory regression objects for every implementation of the global certificate algorithm.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=49/25\), \(k=\sqrt{3/10}\), and \(s=\sqrt{13/10}\), and whiten \(w=(a,b)\) to
\[
 z=\left(a/\sqrt{1/8},b/\sqrt{3/20}\right).
\tag{1}
\]
Every displayed row of every \(F_v\) has Euclidean norm one.  If \(h\in D_v\), both inward standardized facet means are nonnegative.  Thus the union bound gives
\[
 P_h\{v\notin Q_q(W)\}
 \leq2\Phi(-q).
\tag{2}
\]
Rational interval evaluation of \((2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_q^\infty e^{-x^2/2}\,dx\), using range-reduced exponential series on rational subintervals and bounding each remainder by the first omitted alternating term, gives
\[
 0.0249978951482<\Phi(-49/25)<0.0249978951483.
\tag{3}
\]
Therefore \(2\Phi(-49/25)<0.0499957902966<1/20\).  Equations (2)--(3) prove global \(0.95\) coverage, including all equality faces.

Now let \(h\in H_2\) have unique label \(v\).  Since the other three cones form the complement of the interior of \(D_v\), and \(D_v\) is the intersection of its two unit inward halfspaces, distance at least two from every rival implies that both standardized inward facet means are at least two.  If both observed inward coordinates exceed \(q\), the opposite facet of every rival is below \(-q\), so \(Q_q(W)=\{v\}\).  The correlations of the two inward noises are either \(0\) or \(\sqrt{3/13}\), and hence are at least
\[
 \rho_*=-\sqrt{3/13}.
\tag{4}
\]
With \(t=2-q=1/25\), monotonicity of the bivariate Gaussian lower-orthant probability in its correlation follows by differentiating its density integral with respect to the correlation.  It gives
\[
 P_h\{Q_q(W)=\{v\}\}\geq\Phi_2(t,t;\rho_*).
\tag{5}
\]
Direct differentiation along the diagonal yields
\[
 \frac{d}{du}\Phi_2(u,u;\rho_*)
 =2\phi(u)\Phi\left(u\sqrt{\frac{1-\rho_*}{1+\rho_*}}\right)
 \geq\phi(u),\qquad u\geq0.
\tag{6}
\]
The centered integral in polar coordinates is
\[
 \Phi_2(0,0;\rho_*)
 =\frac14-\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}.
\tag{7}
\]
Integrating (6) from \(0\) to \(t\), and using \(0\leq\ell\leq1\), proves
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_2}E_h\ell\{Q_q(W)\}
 \leq\frac34+\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}
 -\{\Phi(1/25)-1/2\}.
\tag{8}
\]
The alternating series for \(\arctan x\) at \(x=\sqrt{3/10}<1\), together with the same outward Gaussian integral calculation used in (3), gives
\[
 0.0797514300099<\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}<0.0797514300101,
\tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 0.0159534368527<\Phi(1/25)-\frac12<0.0159534368530.
\tag{10}
\]
The right side of (8) is therefore below \(0.8137979931574<0.813799\).

For the lower certificate, set \(\mu_\pm=(\pm1/\sqrt2,2)\) and \(\mu_0=(0,2)\).  In whitened coordinates, \(\mu_+\) is at standardized distance two from the rival halfspace across \(a=0\), and at distance greater than two from the remaining rival cones; symmetry gives the same conclusion for \(\mu_-\).  Hence \(\mu_\pm\in H_2\).  After integrating the common second coordinate, write the standardized first coordinate as \(z\).  The risk-mixture density divided by \(\phi(z)\) equals
\[
 \frac{\phi(z-2)+\phi(z+2)}{2\phi(z)}=e^{-2}\cosh(2z).
\tag{11}
\]
Under the discrete label metric, pointwise minimization over actions in the displayed dual reduces to the minimum of this risk-mixture density and \(\lambda\phi(z)\): a singleton \(02\) or \(12\) costs \(\lambda\phi(z)\), while an action containing both costs the risk density, and all other actions are weakly more expensive.  Put
\[
 a_0=1028/625,\qquad \lambda_0=e^{-2}\cosh(2a_0).
\tag{12}
\]
The two curves cross at \(z=\pm a_0\), so the dual value at \(\lambda_0\) is
\[
 D_0=\Phi(a_0-2)-\Phi(-a_0-2)
 +\lambda_0\{2\Phi(-a_0)-1/10\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Outward rational exponential and Gaussian series, with the remainder rule used in (3), give
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 1.8181887545408<\lambda_0<1.8181887545411,\\
 0.3612198823625<\Phi(a_0-2)<0.3612198823627,\\
 0.0001337999106<\Phi(-a_0-2)<0.0001337999108,\\
 0.0500055310938<\Phi(-a_0)<0.0500055310941.
 \end{gathered}
\tag{14}
\]
Substitution into (13) yields \(D_0>0.3611061955936\).  For two multipliers \(\lambda,\lambda'\), the pointwise minimum is Lipschitz in the coverage density, and the penalty contributes \(|\lambda-\lambda'|/10\); hence
\[
 |D(\lambda)-D(\lambda')|\leq\frac{11}{10}|\lambda-\lambda'|.
\tag{15}
\]
The first line of (14) and \(\lambda_4=90909437727/50000000000\) make the right side of (15) smaller than \(3753/10^{15}\).  Therefore
\[
 L_4=D(\lambda_4)>0.3611061955898>0.361100.
\tag{16}
\]
The atomic-duality theorem makes (16) a valid minimax lower certificate.

Finally take \(r=0\).  All four regions meet at the origin, so global honesty gives
\[
 E_0|K(W)|=\sum_{v\in V_4}P_0\{v\in K(W)\}
 \geq4(1-1/20)=19/5.
\tag{17}
\]
For every \(A\subseteq V_4\),
\[
 |A|\leq1+3\mathbf1\{|A|\geq2\},
\tag{18}
\]
and the discrete diameter is one exactly when \(|A|\geq2\).  Equations (17)--(18) imply \(E_0\ell\{K(W)\}\geq14/15\).  Convolution of a bounded rule with the nonsingular Gaussian density is continuous in the mean by the \(L^1\) translation argument in (16) of the atomic-duality proof.  Unique-label interior means in \(H_0\) approach the origin, so \(R_0(K)\geq14/15\).  The rule \(K_{\mathrm{ct}}\) includes each label with probability \(14/15+1/60=19/20\) and incurs loss one only when it reports \(V_4\), which occurs with probability \(14/15\).  It is globally honest and attains the lower bound.
